items.title: The Secret Compound in Hops That Stops You From Overeating
items.summary: Calocurb discoun! Use 'Dave10' at https://www.calocurb.com/?sca_ref=12201982.nQXoagcp66 to get a discount How Hops Extract Suppresses Hunger, Reduces Cravings, Supports Weight Loss, and Makes Intermittent Fasting Easier Host Dave Asprey sits down with Sarah Kennedy, CEO of Calocurb, to explore the surprising science of hunger suppression, natural GLP-1 activation, intermittent fasting, weight loss, visceral fat reduction, and a patented hops extract that may help people eat less without relying on willpower. The conversation centers on Amarasate, a natural compound derived from New Zealand hops, the same plant used to make beer. Originally investigated through a multimillion-dollar research program, this bitter plant extract activates specialized receptors in the digestive tract that stimulate the body's natural appetite-regulating hormones. Sarah explains how this discovery led to Calocurb, a supplement designed to reduce hunger, control cravings, and make fasting and calorie restriction easier. Dave and Sarah break down the biology of GLP-1, CCK, PYY, ghrelin, and leptin, exploring how these hormones influence hunger, fullness, food cravings, and metabolic health. Unlike injectable GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy, Amarasate works through bitter taste receptors in the gut to stimulate the body's own satiety signaling. They examine why the timing and location of these signals matter, how quickly the extract begins working, and what distinguishes this approach…

items.title: Retatrutide Explained: The Triple Agonist and Its Side Effects
items.summary: Retatrutide is a single peptide that activates three hormone receptors at once: GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. This short covers how it works, what the Phase 2 and Phase 3 TRIUMPH trials have shown for weight loss, and the side effects reported in those trials, from nausea and other GI effects to dysesthesia, heart rate, and blood pressure. Subscribe to Peptide Science Explained for more clear, science-backed breakdowns. Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Retatrutide is an investigational drug and is not FDA-approved. Always consult a licensed healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing any treatment. #retatrutide #peptides #weightloss

items.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

items.title: Survodutide Explained: The GLP-1 and Glucagon Dual Agonist and Its Side Effects
items.summary: Survodutide (BI 456906) is a once-weekly peptide from Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. This short covers how it works on appetite, energy use, and the liver, what the phase 2 obesity and MASH trials and the phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE trials showed for weight, blood sugar, and liver fat, where the phase 3 program stands, and what the trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to treatment discontinuation and serious adverse events. Subscribe to Peptide Science Explained for more clear, science-backed breakdowns. Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Survodutide is not an FDA-approved drug. Always consult a licensed healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing any treatment. #survodutide #GLP1 #peptides

items.title: Amycretin Explained: The GLP-1 and Amylin Peptide in One Molecule, and Its Side Effects
items.summary: Amycretin (now named zenagamtide) is Novo Nordisk's single-molecule peptide that activates both GLP-1 and amylin receptors. This short covers how it is built and how it works on appetite, what the phase 1, phase 1b/2a, and type 2 diabetes phase 2 trials showed for weight and A1C, where the AMAZE phase 3 program stands, and what the trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to withdrawals and serious adverse events. items.title: Epithalon Explained: Telomeres, Melatonin, and What Studies Report on Side Effects
items.summary: Epithalon (also spelled Epitalon) is a synthetic four-amino-acid peptide, Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, built from the makeup of a pineal gland extract. This short covers what the research shows on telomerase and telomere length in human cells, melatonin and daily rhythm in aged monkeys and small human studies, and lifespan results in fruit flies and mice, then what studies and FDA's 2026 review report on side effects and safety concerns. Subscribe to Peptide Science Explained for more clear, science-backed breakdowns. Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only and is not medical advice.
